The Imperial Remnant,[10][11] alternatively capitalized as the Imperial remnant[1][2] and also identified as the Remnant Empire[12] or the neo-Imperial forces[1]—was a large neo-Imperialist[1] polity[2] made up of several holdouts of the fallen Galactic Empire.[3] These holdouts had each refused to comply with the terms of the Galactic Concordance that effectively dissolved the Empire in 5 ABY.[10] Believed by New Republic Intelligence to be nothing more than diffuse patchwork of stalward Imperial warlords unable to pose a threat to the New Republic, debates raged over whether the Imperial Remnant should be considered a singular polity or a number of unrelated factions. Secretly however, the Imperial Remnant was far more cohesive then the New Republic believed, with the various surviving Imperial warlords and potentates transmitting into a Shadow Council to coordinate their efforts[2] while maintaining the illusion of being unorganized Imperial warlords, thereby hiding their strength.[3]

Upon Grand Admiral Thrawn's return from his exile in the far galaxy,[13] Thrawn waged a campaign against New Republic with Imperial Remnant forces, but was eventually defeated by the New Republic Defense Force. Later, Chalm Plesk, a historian from the University of Coruscant, wrote the highly anticipated book "The Last War Against the Galactic Empire: On Deployment with the New Republic Fleet" which covered Thrawn's campaign, but its publication was blocked by military figures in the New Republic until the Hosnian Cataclysm. Beaumont Kin would later mention the book as well as Thrawn's Campaign in his own book "The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire"[1]

Behind the scenes

Continuity

The Imperial Remnant[10] first appeared in the current Star Wars canon, albeit unidentified, in "Chapter 1: The Mandalorian,"[14] the premiere episode of the first season of the Disney+ live-action TV show Star Wars: The Mandalorian, which aired November 12, 2019.[15] The Imperial Remnant was subsequently identified as such in the 2020 reference book The Star Wars Book[10] written by Pablo Hidalgo, Cole Horton, and Dan Zehr,[16] which identified the Imperial Remnant as the "Rogue members of the Galactic Empire who refuse to abide by the surrender of the Galactic Concordance and who operate from the fringes of space."[10]

Previously, the term "Imperial remnant" (notably lowercase) had been used in Chuck Wendig's 2017 novel Aftermath: Empire's End, where the term was used to refer to the forces of the Galactic Empire following the Battle of Endor unified under the command of the Shadow Council and self-proclaimed Counselor to the Empire Gallius Rax, all of which was dissolved after the Empire's last stand at the Battle of Jakku.[17] Doctor Chris Kempshall's 2024 reference book Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire later used this non-capitalized version of the name when referring to the Imperial Remnant seen in Star Wars: The Mandalorian.[1]

In the 2026 reference book Star Wars: The Mandalorian Visual Guide written by Pablo Hidalgo, the description for the Imperial remnant includes mentions of Imperial warlords seizing territory in the wake of the Battle of Endor requiring New Republic's concerted efforts to quash and liberate such world, suggesting— though not confirming— that the polity considered to be Imperial remnant may now include the Galactic Empire under the command of Rax and the various other pre-Jakku Imperial holdouts, contradicting The Star Wars Book's earlier definition.[2] Preliminary preview spread pages of the Visual Guide capitalized the name "Imperial Remnant,"[18] while the final version of the book decapitalized the word "remnant."[2] This article currently considers the definition given in the The Star Wars Book to be accurate.

In Star Wars Legends

In the Star Wars Legends continuity, the Imperial Remnant was an oligarchical polity formed in 12 ABY from various holdouts of the Galactic Empire[19] that— under Supreme Commander Gilad Pellaeon[20] and a Council of Moffs[21]— sought to regain control of the galaxy from the New Republic.[20] However, the Remnant was eventually forced to sue for peace with the New Republic in the Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty,[22] and soon joined the Galactic Alliance opposing the Yuuzhan Vong during the Yuuzhan Vong War,[23] until the outbreak of a Second Galactic Civil War resulted in the Remnant leaving the Alliance.[24] The Remnant ultimately would meet its end when it was reformed into the dynastic Fel Empire.[25]
